title: Trace tables
starter: Work out, on paper, what this gives:  total = 0, then add 1, then 2, then 3, then 4. Write down the total after each step.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: What a trace table is
facts: A trace table has one column per variable, plus one for output.
You work through the program line by line, writing down each value as it changes.
This is also called a dry run: running the program in your head.
stations.challenge: Explain why a programmer would trace a program by hand.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A trace table has one column per variable, plus one for output.
Also credit: You work through the program line by line, writing down each value as it changes.

questions.q: What does a trace table record?
questions.a: The value of each variable as the program runs, and anything it outputs

questions.q: Why is it useful for finding logic errors?
questions.a: It shows exactly which line the values first go wrong on

stations.name: Filling one in
facts: Only write a value when it changes, so the table stays readable.
Work strictly line by line, in the order the program actually runs.
Take loops round as many times as the program does, not as many as you expect.
stations.challenge: Trace a short loop by hand and record every change.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Only write a value when it changes, so the table stays readable.
Also credit: Work strictly line by line, in the order the program actually runs.

questions.q: Trace this program and complete the table.
questions.a: row 1: i=, Output=; row 2: total=1, Output=; row 3: total=3, Output=; row 4: total=6, Output=6

questions.q: Why only write a value when it changes?
questions.a: It keeps the table readable and shows clearly where each change happened

stations.name: Tracing a loop
facts: Each time round the loop, write a new row.
Check the loop condition each time before going round again.
The last row shows the values when the loop stops.
stations.challenge: Trace a while loop that halves a number until it reaches one.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Each time round the loop, write a new row.
Also credit: Check the loop condition each time before going round again.

questions.q: Trace this program and complete the table.
questions.a: row 1: Output=; row 2: n=10, count=1, Output=; row 3: n=5, count=2, Output=; row 4: n=2, count=3, Output=; row 5: n=1, count=4, Output=4

questions.q: A while loop's condition is false the first time it is tested. How many rows does the loop add?

stations.name: Tracing selection
facts: At an if statement, decide which branch runs with the current values.
Only the lines in that branch change anything.
Write down which branch was taken if the table has a column for it.
stations.challenge: Trace a program that reports a grade from a mark.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: At an if statement, decide which branch runs with the current values.
Also credit: Only the lines in that branch change anything.

questions.q: Trace this program with a mark of 62 and complete the table.
In an if-elseif-else, how many branches run?

stations.name: Finding the bug with a trace
facts: Trace the program with an input you know the answer for.
Compare each value with what it should be.
The first row where they differ points at the line with the error.
stations.challenge: Trace a faulty program and identify the line that is wrong.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Trace the program with an input you know the answer for.
Also credit: Compare each value with what it should be.

questions.q: This program should output the largest of the three numbers. Trace it and complete the table.
questions.a: row 1: Output=; row 2: largest=9, Output=; row 3: largest=9, Output=9

questions.q: Your trace shows the right values until line 6, where total becomes 12 instead of 10. What does that tell you?

stations.name: Trace tables in the exam
facts: Fill in every row asked for, even if a value repeats.
Put the output in the output column, not in a variable column.
Work slowly: almost all lost marks here come from rushing.
stations.challenge: Complete a full trace table for a given program.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Fill in every row asked for, even if a value repeats.
Also credit: Put the output in the output column, not in a variable column.

questions.q: Trace this program and complete the table.
questions.a: row 1: Output=; row 2: x=4, y=7, Output=; row 3: x=1, y=11, Output=; row 4: x=-2, y=12, Output=12

questions.q: Why is it worth tracing carefully rather than guessing the answer?
questions.a: Marks are given for the intermediate values, not just the final output

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: State what is meant by a trace table.
points: A trace table has one column per variable, plus one for output.
Only write a value when it changes, so the table stays readable.
Write down which branch was taken if the table has a column for it.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
